criteria.title: Use the caller's current agency and permissions
failureModes: A caller supplies another agency's ID or retains revoked permissions.
A long-lived connection keeps authority after account changes.
acceptance: Derive agency and capabilities from current stored identity; never trust a target ID as authority.
Prove foreign-agency, revoked-version and long-lived-session refusal through real registered routes; review deployed identity configuration.

criteria.title: Keep every record read and change inside its agency
failureModes: A new join, bulk update, nested resource or report omits agency scope.
An inconsistent person and owner pairing releases or changes records.
acceptance: Maintain a complete route and data-release inventory, including absence of enabled optional features.
Run cross-agency success/refusal matrices for reads, writes, joins, bulk paths and derived projections; refusal leaves no effects.

criteria.title: Enforce consistent agency ownership in stored data
failureModes: Valid IDs from separate agencies are combined in one relationship.
Direct writes or pooled connection state bypass the chosen database boundary.
acceptance: Record and prove a shared, separate-database or hybrid tenancy decision; RLS is one option rather than an automatic requirement.
Use appropriate composite relationships, constrained write owners or equivalent controls; test raw writes, migrations and connection reuse under the intended principal.

criteria.title: Keep files, caches, search and exports inside their agency
failureModes: A cache key, search index, blob path, signed URL or temporary export lacks trusted agency scope.
Account switching, background refresh or a stale client result retains another agency's data.
acceptance: Inventory every secondary store and document absent features; use trusted agency plus resource/version keys and scoped permissions.
Test cache poisoning, URL replay, search filters, temporary-file cleanup, export downloads and account changes; prove enabled storage access in deployment.

criteria.title: Use the right clearinghouse account for every file and response
failureModes: Agency A's retained bytes use B's credential, account or claim namespace.
A status or ERA receipt advances the wrong account or feed cursor.
acceptance: Bind agency, account, generation, credential reference, remote claim identity and independent feed cursors at selection and execution.
Test cross-account and cross-agency refusal with no partial effects, credential rotation and namespace collisions; retain account-specific vendor acceptance.

criteria.title: Give each eligible agency a bounded worker turn
failureModes: A large early agency backlog indefinitely delays a small later agency.
Multiple accounts or repeated restarts let one agency dominate selection.
acceptance: Define eligible healthy lanes, finite scheduling bounds, per-turn and total-pass budgets, and durable or proved restart continuation.
Prove B's service bound under sustained A backlog, multiple A accounts, inactive lanes and restart; state shared-outage conditions explicitly.

criteria.title: Keep one agency's recoverable failure from stopping others
failureModes: A missing key, poisoned row or failed agency sweep prevents later healthy work.
A slow response body holds shared coordination or retries forever.
acceptance: Use explicit whole-attempt deadlines, safe per-lane backoff and recoverable exception boundaries; separate account faults from shared outages.
Inject preflight, slow-header/body, malformed-response and first-agency sweep failures; B progresses and unsent work never becomes falsely uncertain.

criteria.title: Limit expensive requests by trusted agency
failureModes: A valid user exhausts CPU, parsing memory or query/export capacity.
Unbounded waiting queues move overload from the database to the API.
acceptance: Apply bounded admission/concurrency and endpoint-specific byte, page, query and runtime budgets using validated agency/actor.
Test overload responses, bounded queue/memory, cancellation and costly authorized work while healthy B performs ordinary case management.

criteria.title: Respect shared service and provider capacity
failureModes: Per-agency workers multiply requests beyond a provider-wide quota.
A common breaker or shared plan throttles healthy tenants without visible cause.
acceptance: Map quota scope by service, credential, account, endpoint and deployment using dated primary evidence; cap aggregate work across hosts.
Preserve required global limits while fairly sharing permits; test throttling, delayed recovery and half-open probes without a retry storm.

criteria.title: Coordinate worker selection across separate hosts
failureModes: Two hosts run the same work or treat local semaphores as global limits.
A stale lease holder resumes after expiry or reset and changes newer work.
acceptance: Document lock keys/order and lease scope; enforce same-work exclusion and aggregate limits with database or equivalent durable coordination.
Use independent hosts with real SQL for races, lock loss, lease expiry, cancellation and reset; refuse stale owners and release resources safely.

criteria.title: Preserve ordinary case-management response time
failureModes: Background jobs, reports or exports consume the capacity needed by case managers.
Saturation is hidden by averages or tested only on an empty local database.
acceptance: Define supported agencies, data sizes and latency/error objectives, then reserve or prioritize interactive capacity.
Measure baseline and contended B tail latency, throughput, SQL waits, connections, memory and rejected work under repeatable load and fault conditions.

criteria.title: Use the correct agency's settings and business dates
failureModes: A global clock, setting or cached projection silently applies A's policy to B.
Day rollover, DST or ownership transfer leaves stale obligations and work decisions.
acceptance: Use authoritative agency settings and the recorded supported timezone policy; preserve one shared owner for business rules.
Test two agencies with different settings, date boundaries, DST, rollover, settings changes and stale projections without wall-clock sleeps.

criteria.title: Provision, change and close an agency safely
failureModes: Provisioning leaves partial accounts, permissions, credentials or defaults.
Closure, transfer or restoration loses held records or revives stale access.
acceptance: Define repeatable provisioning, suspension, transfer, export, retention/hold and offboarding procedures without reusing tenant identifiers.
Rehearse partial failure and replay, cross-agency transfer approval, revocation, tenant-specific recovery and cleanup under least privilege.

criteria.title: Keep support and administrative access accountable
failureModes: Support authority becomes unrestricted clinical access or hides cross-agency actions.
An agency administrator can select or export another agency's operational evidence.
acceptance: Preserve the separate narrowly scoped support identity and define privileged access, approval and immutable action evidence.
Test role escalation, cross-agency diagnostics, admin export and emergency access; verify deployed access and review records.

criteria.title: Recognize a repeated action with a lasting request identity
failureModes: A successful request loses its reply and a retry creates another business record.
A retry key is reused for a changed payload or another agency.
acceptance: Inventory mutation operations and scope durable keys by trusted agency, operation and documented actor/resource boundaries; persist a versioned canonical request fingerprint.
Same key and same request returns the retained result; changed request conflicts; key reuse across tenants cannot disclose or merge results. Cover note creation as well as generation.

criteria.title: Give competing repeats one lasting effect
failureModes: Two simultaneous retries both pass a check-then-insert guard.
Process memory recognizes duplicates until a restart or another host.
acceptance: Use durable unique identities and atomic claim/result transitions rather than a check in memory.
Race independent hosts against the same scoped key and payload; inject commit ambiguity, restart and conflict, and assert one business effect and a truthful replay result.

criteria.title: Refuse stale changes and keep related writes together
failureModes: Two approvals or edits silently overwrite each other.
A refused workflow leaves forms, claims or audit rows committed independently.
acceptance: Use current scope, explicit expected revisions and database compare-and-write guards inside the correct aggregate transaction.
Prove stale writes conflict, rollback leaves no partial official effects, and targeted agency/owner/period locks coordinate separate hosts. Document conditional HTTP mapping.

criteria.title: Save the work request before contacting another service
failureModes: Business data commits but the background intent disappears.
An event is published although its related transaction rolled back.
acceptance: For each external/background effect, commit the business transition and durable intent together; record audit in that transaction where required.
Inject failures before/after commit and before delivery; replay the outbox safely. Document compensating steps where multiple stores cannot commit atomically.

criteria.title: Stop an old worker from acting after replacement
failureModes: An expired worker resumes after a replacement already acted.
Cancellation, transaction retry or lock loss repeats an external effect.
acceptance: Define lease ownership, fencing/compare-and-write tokens, expiry and recovery for each worker; never wrap external effects in generic transaction retries.
Pause the original holder through expiry, restart another host, then resume the original; prove stale writes and duplicate sends are refused.

criteria.title: Hold uncertain external sends for reconciliation
failureModes: A timeout is treated as proof of nonreceipt and the claim is sent again.
The vendor accepts but local receipt persistence fails or the host dies.
acceptance: Commit Sending before the external call and preserve Sending/OutcomeUnknown as quarantine; reconcile exact retained identities/evidence before any separately authorized resend.
Inject accepted-but-reply-lost and accepted-but-commit-failed paths plus restart; no blind replay. Retain account-specific reconciliation acceptance.

criteria.title: Prevent another original claim after one was accepted
failureModes: A new generation key produces another original after earlier acceptance.
A correction or replacement is presented as an unrelated original.
acceptance: Enforce original/correction/replacement lifecycle centrally across generation, queueing, dispatch and reconciliation; business identity supplements transport keys.
Prove accepted-original then fresh-key is refused or routed through the permitted correction path, without unsafe concurrent loopholes; certify the vendor duplicate policy.

criteria.title: Repeat required billing checks before sending
failureModes: A queued frozen file remains eligible after attestation withdrawal or a material source change.
A pre-send guard and changing source race so stale authority escapes.
acceptance: Define material changes requiring a hold and enforce the complete applicable documentation/compliance policy at external release, while preserving frozen bytes and amendments.
Revoke attestation, change eligibility and race a hold between generation/queue/send; assert held unsent state, immutable evidence and accurate authorized recovery.

criteria.title: Apply incoming receipts once and track each feed
failureModes: A repeated webhook/receipt creates another payment or status event.
The cursor advances before all effects commit, skipping data forever.
acceptance: Bind inbox/dedup identity to trusted provider/account/agency/feed; authenticate and bound callbacks if introduced; commit retained effects and cursor together.
Test duplicate/re-enveloped/reordered/altered messages, replay after rollback and concurrent processors; unsupported or unmatched pages fail closed without advancing.

criteria.title: Retry only when the effect is safe and the budget allows
failureModes: Nested retries multiply traffic and hold scarce resources.
A validation failure, stale conflict or uncertain send is repeatedly retried as transient.
acceptance: Maintain an operation-specific retry matrix with whole-operation deadlines, capped exponential delay/jitter and aggregate budgets; respect trusted retry guidance.
Test safe read/replay, known-unsent failure, terminal refusal, throttling, shared outage and recovery; cancellation releases connections and permits without claiming no remote effect.

criteria.title: Deliver signature copies and notifications without unsafe repeats
failureModes: A lost mail-provider response creates another invitation or copy.
A stale signer/document or exhausted retry publishes invalid content.
acceptance: Preserve generation-scoped outbox identity, durable provider operation, leases, attempt caps and stale-document/signer guards; reconcile uncertainty rather than blind resend.
Race two workers and change signer/source state at each boundary; test provider ambiguity, cancel/restart, lease expiry and exact authorized copy recovery.

criteria.title: Keep repeat identities for the supported lifetime
failureModes: An expired dedup record permits a late original or restores an obsolete result.
A schema/client change computes a different fingerprint for the same operation.
acceptance: Define maximum retry/redelivery/restore horizons, versioned fingerprints and immutable operation-result retention; unresolved sends are not silently expired.
Test near/after-expiry replay, restore and mixed-version keys; an expired key never silently represents permission for another business effect.

criteria.title: Reconcile external effects after a restore or rollback
failureModes: A database restore forgets accepted sends, payments or consumed keys.
Old binaries or a restored cursor replay external effects that already happened.
acceptance: Before reopening writers, reconcile retained external identities, later valid records, receipts, outbox/inbox and replay keys; define read-only/recovery restrictions.
Run an approved full-service drill spanning external acceptance and restored history; retain reconciliation, prevented duplicate and resumed-operation evidence.

criteria.title: Tell clients accurately whether an action succeeded
failureModes: A 202 response is described as completed work or a failed save leads to an action on stale stored content.
Generic errors cause clients to resubmit with fresh keys or reveal sensitive details.
acceptance: Document operation states, polling/replay and typed safe errors; preserve an operation's key across uncertainty and require refetch/review after revision conflict.
Test lost replies, rejected save then submit, duplicate-key conflict and incompatible client handling; expose safe correlation without narratives or secrets.

criteria.title: Use a separately approved cloud Production environment
failureModes: Demo settings or a personal working PHI database are treated as a customer production deployment.
Wrong endpoint, database, identity, key or backup crosses the environment boundary.
acceptance: Provision an approved Production topology with separate environment identities, credentials, keys, storage, logs, backups and administrative access.
Prove wrong-environment failures through desktop/API/jobs, review current deployment and distinguish synthetic gates from live-customer approval.

criteria.title: Prove deployed permissions and secret boundaries
failureModes: Managed identity exists but has excessive SQL, blob, key or log permissions.
A credential rotation or pooled tenant context grants access to unrelated data.
acceptance: Review intended and actual principals/grants/denies, network boundaries and environment-bound key/storage access; no client database credentials.
Exercise permitted and forbidden actions under deployed identities using approved synthetic probes; rehearse rotation, revocation and key unavailability without PHI disclosure.

criteria.title: Obtain independent security and tenant assurance
failureModes: Internal green tests are mistaken for a complete tenant-security review.
An unreviewed release path or new dependency introduces an unnoticed boundary.
acceptance: Review every enabled release and administration path, attack surface, tenancy decision and deployed control; record residual risks with accountable owners.
Retain independent findings, reproducible negative tests and remediation acceptance; refresh after material architecture/security changes.

criteria.title: Restore a complete usable service within agreed limits
failureModes: A SQL backup restores but keys, files, identity or valid later writes do not.
The recovery time and permitted data loss have never been measured.
acceptance: Set agency-approved RPO/RTO and dependencies, restore SQL/key/blob/service, perform cutover and reconcile later records/external outcomes.
Run an approved synthetic drill, verify usable workflows and record measured time, recovered identities, rejected stale access and recovery sign-off.

criteria.title: Detect failed or missing work and reach an owner
failureModes: A worker, watchdog or incident sink fails silently while readiness stays healthy.
An alert rule exists but no person receives, acknowledges or escalates it.
acceptance: Detect missing outcomes and useful agency/feed progress through independent monitoring, safe scoped signals and explicit thresholds.
Activate the owner-approved rules, induce safe failure/missing-job/poison/starvation cases, retain actual delivery and response evidence; sleeping Demo detection delay is explicit.

criteria.title: Keep complete activity records and safe error logs
failureModes: Ordinary note changes or privileged failures leave no required action audit.
Full exception messages or metric labels reveal PHI, credentials or vendor payloads.
acceptance: Maintain an action/read/deny/export policy and coverage inventory, atomic required evidence and deployed tamper/access protections.
Close R4/R5; inject synthetic secret/narrative sentinels through all enabled sinks, test audit failure/no release, bounded labels and retention/access under actual principals.

criteria.title: Rehearse incidents and degraded service for agencies
failureModes: A shared SQL/vendor/key outage has no usable degraded mode or response plan.
Staff see misleading success or operators bypass holds to clear backlog.
acceptance: Define severity, owner/escalation, tenant notification, safe degraded functions, backlog recovery and continuity procedures.
Exercise database/vendor/storage/key/network failure, containment, recovery and agency communication with synthetic records; retain acknowledgment and closure evidence.

criteria.title: Release compatible versions and rehearse rollback
failureModes: A fingerprint warning permits an incompatible client to change records.
Rolling back binaries is mistaken for reversing a schema or external send.
acceptance: Define supported client/API/schema versions and admission rules, controlled migrations and expand/contract paths with independently usable repair tools.
Test old/new pairs, interrupted update and rollback under synthetic data; incompatible writes fail predictably and evidence identities remain intact.

criteria.title: Preserve records through retention, holds and agency closure
failureModes: A purge/export/offboarding action removes held records or backup evidence.
Policy-only retention is described as enforced operational preservation.
acceptance: Approve applicable retention/hold/export/discovery policy across SQL, blobs, caches, logs, backups and external evidence; avoid automatic deletion before prerequisites.
Rehearse hold, lawful scoped export and closure/recovery; prove retention execution, archive access and accountable approvals without unapproved PHI copying.

criteria.title: Validate capacity and faults on the intended hosting
failureModes: Local fixture speed is presented as Azure or agency-scale capacity.
A sleeping host or shared-plan/database ceiling breaks promised availability.
acceptance: Document target topology, agency/data/load envelope, budget and SLOs with dated limits; choose shared, partitioned or dedicated resources from evidence.
Measure sustained and burst load, noisy neighbor, scale-out, restart and dependency failure on approved representative hosting; record saturation/recovery and costs.

criteria.title: Keep settings, dependencies and deployments controlled
failureModes: Configuration drift enables a gated transport, wrong environment or broad grant.
An outdated dependency or untrusted/incomplete installer compromises recovery.
acceptance: Inventory dependencies and infrastructure/configuration intent, review drift/patches, protect releases and preserve a tested repair/rollback artifact.
Prove exact-source/package provenance, clean-device update/repair, safe switch defaults and approved drift response without weakening security settings.

criteria.title: Operate accounts, privileged sessions and recovery safely
failureModes: Distributed lockout or session recovery behaves differently across hosts.
An offboarded staff member, administrator or compromised secret retains access.
acceptance: Agree identity/MFA/federation requirements by role, shared abuse controls, enrollment/recovery and privileged access; preserve current security-version revocation.
Test scaled authentication, disable/reset/re-enable, credential/key rotation and long-lived session expiry; retain approved offboarding/recovery and actual identity evidence.

criteria.title: Approve each enabled external integration for real use
failureModes: Synthetic acceptance is described as payer acceptance, inbox delivery or lawful signature use.
Provider duplicate/correction semantics or agreements differ from assumed behavior.
acceptance: For each intended enabled transport, obtain account-specific certification and operating/privacy/security agreements; explicitly gated unavailable features remain unavailable.
Prove supported vendor/payer/copy workflows, duplicate and late-response handling, least privilege and agency approval before enabling real effects.

criteria.title: Keep each release's readiness evidence current and understandable
criteria.owner: Release, documentation and agency acceptance owners
failureModes: A stale score is displayed as the current release or historical criteria are silently rewritten.
Staff cannot understand remaining launch gates or use required workflows accessibly.
acceptance: Append a source-bound release snapshot under an immutable versioned rubric, validate coverage/evidence and show unavailable state on mismatch; review new risks at every material change.

Verify plain-language Settings content, accessible workflows and comparison without invented history; preserve signed-off evidence and expose unresolved blockers. Every catalog change starts a new rubric.

snapshots.summary: Starting assessment of release 1.3.37: agency access checks and some retry protections have recorded tests. We still need to prove that agencies cannot hold up each other's work, that every information boundary is protected, and that the whole service can be operated and recovered safely. Cloud Production is not deployed. This dated assessment uses the architecture review's evidence; it does not establish live operation.
nextSteps: Show that a busy or failing agency cannot hold up another agency.
Prevent duplicate original claims and repeat the required billing checks immediately before sending.
Check that every screen, file and report keeps each agency's information separate, and that activity records and error logs are safe.
Practice recovering the whole service, reaching the person responsible for an alert, and safely returning to an earlier release using made-up data.
Agree how agencies and staff join, lose access and leave, then check the service in its intended hosting environment with an independent reviewer.

assessments.notes: The API checks the caller's current agency and permissions, with passing tests recorded for this release. Independent review and checks of the deployed sign-in setup are still needed.
Many actions restrict records to the right agency. Complete checks of every search, download, export and action affecting many records have not been independently established.
Some linked records must belong to the same agency. Complete protection against inconsistent ownership and overly powerful database access remains unfinished.

There is no complete evidence inventory for agency separation across files, saved search results, temporary copies, exports and information left on the screen. Check existing stores and record unavailable features.
Recorded tests reject the wrong clearinghouse account and track different kinds of responses separately. They use synthetic accounts; real account routing and provider acceptance remain unverified.
Fair turns and a measured maximum wait are planned. The worker currently chooses the oldest queued clearinghouse file across all agencies.
A failed first agency or missing account key can delay healthy agencies. Limits on the full wait and tests showing other agencies continue are still needed.
Some limits on incoming data exist. Limits on each agency's expensive work and on how much work can wait are still needed.
Recorded database tests show separate hosts share one clearinghouse request limit. They do not prove fair agency turns or the provider's actual account limits.
Workers coordinate some resets, sends and scans across hosts. Complete shared-work limits and protection against an interrupted worker returning remain unfinished.
Ordinary staff response time has not been measured while another agency runs costly reports or background work. Define the expected load and measure it.
Shared rules use the supported business date and each agency's note settings. Complete tests of settings changes, date boundaries and stale screens remain needed.
Procedures to create, change, close and recover customer agencies are not established for an approved cloud Production service.
The separate support account is restricted to a small set of actions. Complete checks of deployed support access and accountable cross-agency review remain needed.
Some billing and chat actions recognize repeats. Ordinary note creation still lacks a lasting request identity, so a lost reply can leave a repeat uncertain.
Specific claim, file and receipt protections exist. Complete protection against hosts repeating every kind of action simultaneously is not established.
Recorded database tests show certain schedule and billing changes reject stale updates and keep related work together. They do not cover every workflow or heavy-load condition.
Some background requests and action records are saved safely. Complete records of official actions and saved requests for every changing operation remain unfinished.
Some send and mail workers hold exclusive permission to act. Complete tests of permission expiry, replaced workers and cancellation remain needed.
Recorded tests show uncertain clearinghouse sends are held rather than automatically repeated. Real provider acceptance of the investigation and recovery process remains needed.

The assessment found a missing server rule: a new request key can produce another original claim after earlier acceptance. No duplicate payment was shown; reproduce and repair this before real billing sends.
The assessment found queued sends do not repeat all required documentation and compliance checks. A test where eligibility changes before sending still needs to run.

Recorded tests cover repeated receipts, related updates and response tracking, including rejection of the wrong account. Actual provider completeness and unsupported formats remain outside that evidence.
Current retry and time limits differ by workflow. A complete policy for safe repeats, the full response wait and shared retry limits still needs proof.
Signature mail saves request state, wait times and attempt limits. Complete interruption tests and actual provider delivery and recovery checks remain needed.
Settings define how long some repeat identities are kept. Their relationship to late responses, restoration and different client versions is not established.
A complete recovery drill has not reconciled external actions, valid later records and identities used to recognize repeats.
Some stale-update errors and safe support references exist. Lost note replies, submitting after a failed save and different client versions still have separate gaps.
Cloud Production is not deployed. Demo and the owner's personal local PHI store do not establish an approved production service for multiple agencies.
Service identities and a limited portal permission rehearsal exist. Actual deployed database, key, file, log and network permissions are not independently proven.
Internal source review and targeted tests exist. Independent review of agency access and actual deployed protections is still required.
A guarded Demo restore script and procedure exist. Complete usable-service recovery, switch-over and reconciliation of later records have not been rehearsed.
Watchdog source and alert scripts exist. The assessment found planned rules absent and no established actual alert delivery.
The assessment identifies missing records of ordinary note actions and potentially unsafe full error logging. Complete action evidence and safe diagnostics are required before PHI hosting.
No completed agency-level exercise of shared-service failure, safe reduced service and recovery response was established.
Release tools retain prior packages and controlled migration procedures. Supported app/server/database versions and safe rollback are not fully proven.
Some preservation controls and written policies exist. Actual retention, backup and file preservation, agency closure and export procedures remain incomplete.
Demo has dated evidence of its hosting limits. Measurements of intended Production capacity, faults and competing agencies remain future work.
Manual release and deployment checks exist. Complete proof of consistent settings, maintained dependencies and safe repair after an interrupted installation remains unfinished.
Current accounts can revoke old access after certain changes. Required stronger sign-in controls, shared abuse limits and actual recovery/offboarding checks are not established.
Server billing sends are test-only; vendor and payer acceptance is not established. Real signature and email use also needs separate checks and agreements.
This retrospective baseline starts release tracking; no earlier snapshot exists. This baseline does not count a readiness display or independent accessibility/readiness review as previously shipped.

snapshots.summary: This release's local checks show better handling of a failed agency's background work, stalled clearinghouse responses, day-to-day worker records, billing export checks, and request, incident and health errors. The new Settings view explains the recorded evidence and remaining work. These are bounded tests, not proof of a ready cloud service. Another original claim and complete checks immediately before sending still need repair; complete activity records and safe logs, fair agency turns, recovery and independent review remain open. Cloud Production is not deployed. Installation and publication acceptance is recorded separately in the release record; this assessment alone does not establish deployed operation.
nextSteps: Agree the original-claim rules using recorded receipt and uncertainty history, then enforce them in one shared rule. Complete the current billing checks for the exact claims immediately before sending.
Prove that a busy, failing or newly added agency cannot delay another agency indefinitely. Limit incoming expensive work, waiting work and each background pass.
Check every screen, file, saved result and export for agency separation. Complete ordinary action records and review every enabled error-log channel, including startup and database diagnostics.
Practice full-service recovery, reconciliation of later and external actions, alert delivery and acknowledgment, and safe rollback using approved synthetic data.

Establish approved agency and account lifecycle, deployed permissions, stronger sign-in controls, retention and vendor-use agreements. Measure the intended host under competing-agency load and obtain independent review.

Obtain human accessibility and independent readiness review. Review each later release's installation and publication evidence separately, while keeping cloud Production and real provider activation gated; a score alone does not permit launch.

assessments.notes: The retained October 8 architecture review records checks of the caller's current agency and permissions. These protections remain in the reviewed software. Independent review and checks of the deployed sign-in setup are still needed; the old test record is not a new deployed acceptance run.

The October 8 architecture review records agency restrictions for many actions. Current targeted billing and incident tests preserve their agency boundaries. A complete inventory and independent checks of every search, download, export and action affecting many records remain unfinished.

The October 8 architecture review records some requirements that linked records belong to the same agency. Complete protection against inconsistent ownership, direct database changes and overly powerful database access remains unfinished. This release adds no new storage model or migration.

The October 8 baseline still has no complete evidence inventory for agency separation across files, saved search results, temporary copies, exports and information left on the screen. Check existing stores and record unavailable features; the new note-worker completion cache is only a bounded piece of this inventory.

The retained October 8 architecture-review tests reject the wrong clearinghouse account and track different response feeds separately. Current focused connector and receipt controls preserve those protections using synthetic accounts. Actual account routing, credential rotation and provider acceptance remain unverified.

The October 8 baseline's fair-turn requirement remains planned. Note-worker discovery now finds agencies in groups of at most 100 and retires prior-day completion entries, but total work and waiting time are not bounded. Clearinghouse selection still uses the oldest queued file across agencies; no measured maximum wait for a healthy agency is established.

October 8 failure tests show that a recoverable note-sweep failure rolls back that agency's change and allows a healthy agency to continue, with a later safe retry. Real-connector tests also stop a stalled response at the 45-second exchange deadline and hold an uncertain upload without repeating it. This is bounded local acceptance: clearinghouse preflight failures, per-agency backoff, full-pass limits and live isolation still need work.

The October 8 architecture review records some incoming-data limits. Bounded note-worker discovery and response deadlines do not limit an agency's incoming expensive requests or all waiting work. Controls for how much work each agency can submit or leave waiting, and tests under competing-agency load, remain planned.

The retained October 8 database tests show that separate hosts share one clearinghouse request limit. Current portable deadline controls preserve coordination and cleanup, but they do not repeat the earlier database proof or establish fair turns, actual provider account limits or live capacity.

The retained October 8 database evidence covers selected cross-host reset, send and scan coordination. A later guarded private-database run passed the two note-sweep exclusion and reset-refusal controls; those results are recorded separately from the portable tests. Complete shared-work limits, interrupted-worker replacement and protection against a stale worker returning remain unfinished; no live-host guarantee is claimed.

The October 8 architecture review did not measure ordinary staff response time while another agency runs costly reports or background work. The local paging, cache and deadline repairs do not establish response-time targets under shared load. Define the intended load and measure it.

Shared rules retain the supported business-date policy and each agency's note settings recorded in the October 8 review. New deterministic tests prove that prior-day completion entries are retired, completed agencies are skipped that day, failed agencies can recover, and later days run again. Complete two-agency settings-change, daylight-saving, ownership-change and stale-screen acceptance remains unfinished. Changes during the same day and limits on current-day completion records remain open.

The October 8 baseline's procedures to create, change, close and recover customer agencies remain unestablished for an approved cloud Production service. No live agency lifecycle, retention or recovery exercise was performed for this assessment.

The October 8 architecture review records a separate support account restricted to a small set of actions. Current request and incident controls preserve agency-scoped support references and refuse inappropriate cross-agency or administrative changes. These local controls do not establish complete privileged-action evidence, deployed support permissions, emergency access or independent cross-agency review.

The October 8 architecture review records repeat recognition for selected billing and chat actions. Ordinary note creation still lacks a lasting request identity, so a lost reply can leave a repeat uncertain. The current export repair preserves existing request recognition without completing the full mutation inventory.

The October 8 architecture review records specific claim, file and receipt uniqueness protections. Complete protection against separate hosts repeating every changing operation at the same time, including a lost commit reply and restart, remains unestablished. No broader once-only guarantee is added by this release.

The retained October 8 database tests show that selected schedule and billing changes reject stale updates and keep related work together. Current note, billing and incident tests add bounded rollback and preserved-record controls using synthetic data. They do not cover every workflow, simultaneous database change or heavy-load condition.

The October 8 architecture review records selected saved background requests and action records. Current note and billing tests preserve their existing atomic records; incident tests prove the bounded incident transaction. Complete official-action records and durable saved intent before every external effect remain unfinished.

The October 8 architecture review records selected send and mail workers' exclusive permission to act. This release does not establish the complete permission-expiry, replaced-worker, cancellation and stale-holder acceptance matrix. External effects must not be treated as safely repeatable merely because a local lease expired.

The retained October 8 tests hold uncertain clearinghouse sends for investigation. New real-connector tests observe one physical upload, deadline cancellation while the caller remains active, a retained unknown outcome and no automatic second upload. The earlier database evidence remains separately dated. Real provider investigation, restart and reconciliation acceptance are still needed; a timeout does not prove that the provider received nothing.

The October 8 assessment found a missing server rule: a fresh request key can create another original claim after earlier acceptance. This remains blocked. The next work is bounded fact and policy design covering recorded receipts, uncertainty, confirmed nonreceipt, corrections and malformed history; it is not an implemented guard. Rules for history from different sending modes and rejected claims, shared enforcement and simultaneous database tests are still required before real billing sends.

October 8 fail-first tests now prove that an export and its exact replay are refused when an unrelated required approval is revoked, while retained files and records stay unchanged. The shared gate preserves all remaining compliance errors already identified by the export checks; valid exact exceptions and approved recovery still work. This prerequisite does not close the blocker: queueing and the moment before sending still need the full current eligibility check for the exact retained claim set, correction and void-purpose rules, and simultaneous-change tests.

The retained October 8 architecture-review tests cover repeated receipts, related updates and feed tracking, including wrong-account refusal. Current focused receipt controls preserve those behaviors. Actual provider completeness, all supported formats, concurrent delivery and live recovery remain outside that evidence.

October 8 local tests prove a bounded response wait without automatically repeating an uncertain upload.
